name: MonarchTypingIndicator
title: TypingIndicator
summary: "Ana is typing…" under a conversation, with three decorative bouncing dots, worded for one, two or several people.
whenToUse: Under a message list or a comment thread, while other people are writing.
whenNotToUse: For the presence of people who are not writing use an avatar stack or a status dot. For the progress of a task use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTypingIndicator(names: List<String>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, text: String? = null, reserveSpace: Boolean = true, announceChanges: Boolean = true)

options.name: names
options.description: Who is typing now, as their names should be read, newest last. Leave out the person using the app.

options.name: text
options.description: Replaces the built-in sentence. Ignored while names is empty.

options.name: reserveSpace
options.description: Keeps the height of one line while nobody is typing.

options.name: announceChanges
options.description: Makes the element a polite live region, so each new sentence is announced.

states.name: nobody
states.description: Nothing is drawn. With reserveSpace the height of one line is kept.

states.name: animations off
states.description: The dots stand still in the muted text color.

appearance: The sentence uses the caption type role in the muted text color. Resting dots use the subtle text color and turn to the muted text color at the top of their bounce, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web takes people with an id and a messages object with three functions; Android takes names and one text override, as iOS does. The built-in wording is three string resources. The web fades the dots with opacity; Android moves between two text color roles instead, because Monarch does not dim colors with alpha. The sentence wraps instead of being ellipsized, so it is never cut at a large font size.
accessibility: The dots are decoration; the sentence is one TalkBack element.
The element is a polite live region, so a new sentence is announced without moving focus, unless announceChanges is false.
The element stays in the layout while nobody is typing, so the first sentence after silence is announced as a change.
While nobody is typing the element has no text and TalkBack skips it.
The dots stand still when the user has turned animations off.
The text and the dots grow with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Long names wrap onto more lines; with reserveSpace only one line is held while nobody is typing.
The built-in strings name at most two people; three or more give "Several people are typing…".
Pass the names in the order they should be read; the first two are used.

examples.title: One, two and several people

parityExceptions.reason: The buttons are controls of the web docs page that set the demo state (the count of people typing); they are page chrome, not part of the component.
parityExceptions.convention: docs-page chrome is not part of a native example
